Question: Which of the following statements describe a valid test objective?

Variants.Label: A
Variants.Text: To prove that there are no unfixed defects in the system under test

Variants.Label: B
Variants.Text: To prove that there will be no failures after the implementation of the system into production

Variants.Label: C
Variants.Text: To reduce the risk level of the test object and to build confidence in the quality level

Variants.Label: D
Variants.Text: To verify that there are no untested combinations of inputs

Explanation: C) Is correct. Testing finds defects and failures which reduces the level of risk and at the same time gives more confidence in the quality level of the test object

Question: Which of the following options shows an example of test activities that contribute to success?

Variants.Label: A
Variants.Text: Having testers involved during various software development lifecycle (SDLC) activities will help to detect defects in work products

Variants.Label: B
Variants.Text: Testers try not to disturb the developers while coding, so that the developers write better code

Variants.Label: C
Variants.Text: Testers collaborating with end users help to improve the quality of defect reports during component integration and system testing

Variants.Label: D
Variants.Text: Certified testers will design much better test cases than non-certified testers

Explanation: A) Is correct. It is important that testers are involved from the beginning of the software development lifecycle (SDLC). It will increase understanding of design decisions and will detect defects early.

Question: You have been assigned as a tester to a team producing a new system incrementally. You have noticed that no changes have been made to the existing regression test cases for several iterations and no new regression defects were identified. Your manager is happy, but you are not. Which testing principle explains your skepticism?

Variants.Label: A
Variants.Text: Tests wear out

Variants.Label: B
Variants.Text: Absence-of-errors fallacy

Variants.Label: C
Variants.Text: Defects cluster together

Variants.Label: D
Variants.Text: Exhaustive testing is impossible

Explanation: A) Is correct. This principle means that if the same tests are repeated over and over again, eventually these tests no longer find any new defects. This is probably why the tests all passed in this release as well

Question:
You work in a team that develops a mobile application for food ordering. In the current iteration the team decided to implement the payment functionality. 

Which of the following activities is a part of test analysis?

Variants.Label: A
Variants.Text: Estimating that testing the integration with the payment service will take 8 person-days

Variants.Label: B
Variants.Text: Deciding that the team should test if it is possible to properly share payment between many users

Variants.Label: C
Variants.Text: Using boundary value analysis (BVA) to derive the test data for the test cases that check the correct payment processing for the minimum allowed amount to be paid

Variants.Label: D
Variants.Text: Analyzing the discrepancy between the actual result and expected result after executing a test case that checks the process of payment with a credit card, and reporting a defect

Explanation: B) Is correct. This is an example of defining test conditions which is a part of test analysis

Question:
Which of the following factors have a SIGNIFICANT influence on the test approach? 

i. The SDLC 
ii. The number of defects detected in previous projects 
iii. The identified product risks 
iv. New regulatory requirements forcing formal white-box testing 
v. The test environment setup

Variants.Label: A
Variants.Text: i, ii have significant influence

Variants.Label: B
Variants.Text: i, iii, iv have significant influence

Variants.Label: C
Variants.Text: ii, iv, v have significant influence

Variants.Label: D
Variants.Text: iii, v have significant influence

Explanation:
B) Is correct. 

i. Is true. The SDLC has an influence on the test approach 
ii. Is false. The number of defects detected in previous projects may have some influence, but this is not as significant as i, iii and iv 
iii. Is true. The identified product risks are one of the most important factors influencing the test approach 
iv. Is true. Regulatory requirements are important factors influencing the test approach 
v. Is false. The test environment has no significant influence on the test approach

Question: Which TWO of the following tasks belong MAINLY to a testing role?

Variants.Label: A
Variants.Text: Configure test environments

Variants.Label: B
Variants.Text: Maintain the product backlog

Variants.Label: C
Variants.Text: Design solutions to new requirements

Variants.Label: D
Variants.Text: Create the test plan

Variants.Label: E
Variants.Text: Analyze the test basis

Explanation:
A) Is correct. This is done by the testers 

E) Is correct. This is done by the testers since its technical task done as part of a test analysis.

Question:
Which of the following skills (i-v) are the MOST important skills of a tester? 

i. Having domain knowledge 
ii. Creating a product vision 
iii. Being a good team player 
iv. Planning and organizing the work of the team 
v. Critical thinking

Variants.Label: A
Variants.Text: ii and iv are important

Variants.Label: B
Variants.Text: i, iii and v are important

Variants.Label: C
Variants.Text: i, ii and v are important

Variants.Label: D
Variants.Text: iii and iv are important

Explanation:
B) Is correct. 

i. Is true. Having domain knowledge is an important tester skill 
ii. Is false. This is a task of the business analyst together with the business representative 
iii. Is true. Being a good team player is an important skill 
iv. Is false. Planning and organizing the work of the team is a task of the test manager or, mostly in an Agile software development project, the whole team and not just the tester 
v. Is true. Critical thinking is one of the most important skills of testers

Question: How is the whole team approach present in the interactions between testers and business representatives?

Variants.Label: A
Variants.Text: Business representatives decide on test automation approaches

Variants.Label: B
Variants.Text: Testers help business representatives to define test strategy

Variants.Label: C
Variants.Text: Business representatives are not part of the whole team approach

Variants.Label: D
Variants.Text: Testers help business representatives to create suitable acceptance tests

Explanation: D) Is correct. Testers will work closely with business representatives to ensure that the desired quality levels are achieved. This includes supporting and collaborating with them to help them create suitable acceptance tests

Question: Consider the following rule: “for every SDLC activity there is a corresponding test activity”. In which SDLC models does this rule hold?

Variants.Label: A
Variants.Text: Only in sequential SDLC models

Variants.Label: B
Variants.Text: Only in iterative SDLC models

Variants.Label: C
Variants.Text: Only in iterative and incremental SDLC models

Variants.Label: D
Variants.Text: In sequential, incremental, and iterative SDLC models

Explanation: D) Is correct. This rule holds for all SDLC models

Question: Which of the following statements BEST describes the acceptance test-driven development (ATDD) approach?

Variants.Label: A
Variants.Text: In ATDD, acceptance criteria are typically created based on the given/when/then format

Variants.Label: B
Variants.Text: In ATDD, test cases are mainly created at component testing and are code-oriented

Variants.Label: C
Variants.Text: In ATDD, tests are created, based on acceptance criteria to drive the development of the related software

Variants.Label: D
Variants.Text: in ATDD, tests are based on the desired behavior of the software, which makes it easier for team members to understand them

Explanation: C) Is correct. In acceptance test-driven development (ATDD) tests are written from acceptance criteria as part of the design process

Question: Which of the following is NOT an example of the shift left approach?

Variants.Label: A
Variants.Text: Reviewing the user requirements before they are formally accepted by the stakeholders

Variants.Label: B
Variants.Text: Writing a component test before the corresponding code is written

Variants.Label: C
Variants.Text: Executing a performance efficiency test for a component during component testing

Variants.Label: D
Variants.Text: Writing a test script before setting up the configuration management process

Explanation: D) Is correct. Test scripts should be subject to configuration management, so it makes no sense to create the test scripts before this process is set up

Question: Which of the arguments below would you use to convince your manager to organize retrospectives at the end of each release cycle?

Variants.Label: A
Variants.Text: Retrospectives are very popular these days and clients would appreciate it if we added them to our processes

Variants.Label: B
Variants.Text: Organizing retrospectives will save the organization money because without them end user representatives do not provide immediate feedback about the product

Variants.Label: C
Variants.Text: Process weaknesses identified during the retrospective can be analyzed and serve as a to do list for the organization’s continuous process improvement program

Variants.Label: D
Variants.Text: Retrospectives embrace five values including courage and respect, which are crucial to maintain continuous improvement in the organization

Explanation: C) Is correct. Regularly conducted retrospectives, when appropriate follow up activities occur, are critical to continual improvement of development and testing

Question:
Which types of failures (1-4) fit which test levels (A-D) BEST? 

1. Failures in system behavior as it deviates from the user’s business needs 
2. Failures in communication between components 
3. Failures in logic in a module 
4. Failures in not correctly implemented business rules 

A. Component testing 
B. Component integration testing 
C. System testing 
D. Acceptance testing
Explanation:
A) Is correct. 

Considering: 
• The test basis for acceptance testing is the user’s business needs (1D) 
• Communication between components is tested during component integration testing (2B) 
• Failures in logic can be found during component testing (3A) 
• Business rules are the test basis for system testing (4C)

Question:
You are testing a user story with three acceptance criteria: AC1, AC2 and AC3. AC1 is covered by test case TC1, AC2 by TC2, and AC3 by TC3. The test execution history had three test runs on three consecutive versions of the software as follows:

Tests are repeated once you are informed that all defects found in the test run are corrected and a new version of the software is available. 

Which of the above tests are executed as regression tests?

Variants.Label: B
Variants.Text: Only 5, 7

Variants.Label: D
Variants.Text: Only 5, 6

Explanation:
B) Is correct. Because TC1 and TC3 failed in Execution 1 (i.e., test (1) and test (3)), test (4) and test (6) are confirmation tests. 
Because TC2 and TC3 failed in Execution 2 (i.e., tests (5) and (6)), test (8) and test (9) are also confirmation tests. 
TC2 passed in Execution 1 (i.e., test (2)), so test (5) is a regression test. 
TC1 passed in the Execution 2 (i.e., test (4)), so test (7) is also a regression test.

Question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of static testing?

Variants.Label: A
Variants.Text: Having less expensive defect management due to the ease of detecting defects later in the SDLC

Variants.Label: B
Variants.Text: Fixing defects found during static testing is generally much less expensive than fixing defects found during dynamic testing

Variants.Label: C
Variants.Text: Finding coding defects that might not have been found by only performing dynamic testing

Variants.Label: D
Variants.Text: Detecting gaps and inconsistencies in requirements

Explanation: A) Is correct. Defect management is no less expensive. Finding and fixing defects later in SDLC is more costly

Question: Which of the following is a benefit of early and frequent feedback?

Variants.Label: A
Variants.Text: It improves the test process for future projects

Variants.Label: B
Variants.Text: It forces customers to prioritize their requirements based on agreed risks

Variants.Label: C
Variants.Text: It provides a measure for the quality of changes

Variants.Label: D
Variants.Text: It helps avoid requirements misunderstandings

Explanation: D) Is correct. Early and frequent feedback can prevent misunderstandings about requirements

Question:
The reviews being used in your organization have the following attributes: 

•There is the role of a scribe 
•The main purpose is to evaluate quality 
•The meeting is led by the author of the work product 
•There is individual preparation 
•A review report is produced 

Which of the following review types is MOST likely being used?

Variants.Label: A
Variants.Text: Informal review

Variants.Label: B
Variants.Text: Walkthrough

Variants.Label: C
Variants.Text: Technical review

Variants.Label: D
Variants.Text: Inspection

Explanation:
B) Is correct. Considering the attributes: 
• Specified for walkthroughs, technical reviews, and inspections; thus, the reviews being performed cannot be informal reviews 
• The purpose of evaluating quality is one of the most important objectives of a walkthrough 
• This is not allowed for inspections and is typically not done in technical reviews. A moderator is needed in walkthroughs and is allowed for informal reviews 
• All types of reviews can include individual preparation (even informal reviews) 
• All types of reviews can produce a review report, although informal reviews do not require documentation

Question: Which of these statements is NOT a factor that contributes to successful reviews?

Variants.Label: A
Variants.Text: Participants should dedicate adequate time for the review

Variants.Label: B
Variants.Text: Splitting large work products into small parts to make the required effort less intense

Variants.Label: C
Variants.Text: Participants should avoid behaviors that might indicate boredom, exasperation, or hostility to other participants

Variants.Label: D
Variants.Text: Failures found should be acknowledged, appreciated, and handled objectively

Explanation: D) Is correct. During reviews one can find defects, not failures

Question: Which of the following is a characteristic of experience-based test techniques?

Variants.Label: A
Variants.Text: Test cases are created based on detailed design information

Variants.Label: B
Variants.Text: Items tested within the interface code section are used to measure coverage

Variants.Label: C
Variants.Text: The techniques heavily rely on the tester’s knowledge of the software and the business domain

Variants.Label: D
Variants.Text: The test cases are used to identify deviations from the requirements

Explanation: C) Is correct. This is a common characteristic of experience-based test techniques. This knowledge and experience include expected use of the software, its environment, likely defects, and the distribution of those defects is used to define tests

Question:
You are testing a simplified apartment search form which has only two search criteria: 

• floor (with three possible options: ground floor; first floor; second or higher floor) 
• garden type (with three possible options: no garden; small garden; large garden) 

Only apartments on the ground floor have gardens. The form has a built-in validation mechanism that will not allow you to use the search criteria which violate this rule. 

Each test has two input values: floor and garden type. You want to apply equivalence partitioning (EP) to cover each floor and each garden type in your tests. 

What is the minimal number of test cases to achieve 100% EP coverage?
Explanation:
B) Is correct. “Small garden” and “large garden” can go only with “ground floor”, so we need two test cases with “ground floor” which cover these two “garden type” partitions. We need two more test cases to cover the two other “floor” partitions and a remaining ”garden type” partition of “no garden”. 

We need a total of four test cases: 
TC1 (ground floor, small garden) 
TC2 (ground floor, large garden) 
TC3 (first floor, no garden) 
TC4 (second or higher floor, no garden)

Question:
You are testing a system that calculates the final course grade for a given student. 

The final grade is assigned based on the final result, according to the following rules: 
• 0 – 50 points: failed 
• 51 – 60 points: fair 
• 61 – 70 points: satisfactory 
• 71 – 80 points: good 
• 81 – 90 points: very good 
• 91 – 100 points: excellent 

You have prepared the following set of test cases: 

What is the 2-value Boundary Value Analysis (BVA) coverage for the final result that is achieved with the existing test cases?
Explanation:
A) Is correct. 

There are 12 boundary values for the final result values: 0, 50, 51, 60, 61, 70, 71, 80, 81, 90, 91, and 100. 
The test cases cover six of them (TC1 – 91, TC2 – 50, TC3 – 81, TC4 – 60, TC5 – 70 and TC7 – 51). 
Therefore, the test cases cover 6/12 = 50%.

Question:
Your favorite bicycle daily rental store has just introduced a new Customer Relationship Management system and asked you, one of their most loyal members, to test it. 

The implemented features are as follows: 
• Anyone can rent a bicycle, but members receive a 20% discount 
• However, if the return deadline is missed, the discount is no longer available 
• After 15 rentals, members get a gift: a T-Shirt 

Decision table describing the implemented features looks as follows: 

Based ONLY on the feature description of the Customer Relationship Management system, which of the above rules describes an impossible situation?

Variants.Label: A
Variants.Text: R4

Variants.Label: B
Variants.Text: R2

Variants.Label: C
Variants.Text: R6

Variants.Label: D
Variants.Text: R8

Explanation: D) Is correct. No discount as a non-member that has also missed a deadline, but only members can receive a gift T-Shirt. Hence, the action is not correct

Question:
You test a system whose lifecycle is modeled by the state transition diagram shown below. The system starts in the INIT state and ends its operation in the OFF state. 

What is the MINIMAL number of test cases to achieve valid transitions coverage?
Explanation:
D) Is correct. 

“test” and “error” transitions cannot occur in one test case. 
Neither can both “done” transitions. 
This means we need at least three test cases to achieve transition coverage. 

For example: 
TC1: test, done 
TC2: run, error, done 
TC3: run, pause, resume, pause, done

Question: Your test suite achieved 100% statement coverage. What is the consequence of this fact?

Variants.Label: A
Variants.Text: Each instruction in the code that contains a defect has been executed at least once

Variants.Label: B
Variants.Text: Any test suite containing more test cases than your test suite will also achieve 100% statement coverage

Variants.Label: C
Variants.Text: Each path in the code has been executed at least once

Variants.Label: D
Variants.Text: Every combination of input values has been tested at least once

Explanation: A) Is correct. Since 100% statement coverage is achieved, every statement, including the ones with defects, must have been executed and evaluated at least once

Question: Which of the following is NOT true for white-box testing?

Variants.Label: A
Variants.Text: During white-box testing the entire software implementation is considered

Variants.Label: B
Variants.Text: White-box coverage metrics can help identify additional tests to increase code coverage

Variants.Label: C
Variants.Text: White-box test techniques can be used in static testing

Variants.Label: D
Variants.Text: White-box testing can help identify gaps in requirements implementation

Explanation: D) Is correct. This is the weakness of the white-box test techniques. They are not able to identify the missing implementation, because they are based solely on the test object structure, not on the requirements specification

Question: Which of the following BEST describes the concept behind error guessing?

Variants.Label: A
Variants.Text: Error guessing involves using your knowledge and experience of defects found in the past and typical errors made by developers

Variants.Label: B
Variants.Text: Error guessing involves using your personal experience of development and the errors you made as a developer

Variants.Label: C
Variants.Text: Error guessing requires you to imagine that you are the user of the test object and to guess errors the user could make interacting with it

Variants.Label: D
Variants.Text: Error guessing requires you to rapidly duplicate the development task to identify the sort of errors a developer might make

Explanation: A) Is correct. The basic concept behind error guessing is that the tester tries to guess what errors may have been made by the developer and what defects may be in the test object based on past experience (and sometimes checklists)

Question:
In your project there has been a delay in the release of a brand-new application and test execution started late, but you have very detailed domain knowledge and good analytical skills. The full list of requirements has not yet been shared with the team, but management is asking for some test results to be presented. 

Which test technique fits BEST in this situation?

Variants.Label: A
Variants.Text: Checklist-based testing

Variants.Label: B
Variants.Text: Error guessing

Variants.Label: C
Variants.Text: Exploratory testing

Variants.Label: D
Variants.Text: Branch testing

Explanation: C) Is correct. Exploratory testing is most useful when there are few known specifications and/or there is a pressing timeline for testing

Question: Which of the following BEST describes the way acceptance criteria can be documented?

Variants.Label: A
Variants.Text: Performing retrospectives to determine the actual needs of the stakeholders regarding a given user story

Variants.Label: B
Variants.Text: Using the given/when/then format to describe an example test condition related to a given user story

Variants.Label: C
Variants.Text: Using verbal communication to reduce the risk of misunderstanding the acceptance criteria by others

Variants.Label: D
Variants.Text: Documenting risks related to a given user story in a test plan to facilitate the risk-based testing of a given user story

Explanation: B) Is correct. This is the standard way to document acceptance criteria

Question:
Consider the following user story: 

As an Editor 
I want to review content before it is published 
so that I can assure the grammar is correct 

and its acceptance criteria: 
• The user can log in to the content management system with "Editor" role 
• The editor can view existing content pages 
• The editor can edit the page content 
• The editor can add markup comments 
• The editor can save changes 
• The editor can reassign to the "content owner" role to make updates 

Which of the following is the BEST example of an ATDD test for this user story?

Variants.Label: A
Variants.Text: Test if the editor can save the document after edit the page content

Variants.Label: B
Variants.Text: Test if the content owner can log in and make updates to the content

Variants.Label: C
Variants.Text: Test if the editor can schedule the edited content for publication

Variants.Label: D
Variants.Text: Test if the editor can reassign to another editor to make updates

Explanation: A) Is correct. This test covers two acceptance criteria: one about editing the document and one about saving changes

Question: How do testers add value to iteration and release planning?

Variants.Label: A
Variants.Text: Testers determine the priority of the user stories to be developed

Variants.Label: B
Variants.Text: Testers focus only on the functional aspects of the system to be tested

Variants.Label: C
Variants.Text: Testers participate in the detailed risk identification and risk assessment of user stories

Variants.Label: D
Variants.Text: Testers guarantee the release of high-quality software through early test design during the release planning

Explanation: C) Is correct. According to the syllabus, this is one of the ways testers add value to iteration and release planning

Question: Which TWO of the following options are the exit criteria for testing a system?

Variants.Label: A
Variants.Text: Test environment readiness

Variants.Label: B
Variants.Text: The ability to log in to the test object by the tester

Variants.Label: C
Variants.Text: Estimated defect density is reached

Variants.Label: D
Variants.Text: Requirements are translated into given/when/then format

Variants.Label: E
Variants.Text: Regression tests are automated

Explanation: C) Is correct. Estimated defect density is a measure of diligence; hence it belongs to the exit criteria. E) Is correct. Automation of regression tests is a completion criterion; hence it belongs to the exit criteria

Question:
Your team uses the three-point estimation technique to estimate the test effort for a new high-risk feature. The following estimates were made: 
• Most optimistic estimation: 2 person-hours 
• Most likely estimation: 11 person-hours 
• Most pessimistic estimation: 14 person-hours 

What is the final estimate?

Variants.Label: A
Variants.Text: 9 person-hours

Variants.Label: B
Variants.Text: 14 person-hours

Variants.Label: C
Variants.Text: 11 person-hours

Variants.Label: D
Variants.Text: 10 person-hours

Explanation:
D) Is correct. 
E = (optimistic +4•most likely + pessimistic)/6 
E=(2+(4•11)+14)/6=10

Question:
You are testing a mobile application that allows users to find a nearby restaurant based on the type of food they want to eat. Consider the following list of test cases, priorities (i.e., a smaller number means a higher priority), and dependencies: 

Which of the following test cases should be executed as the third one?

Variants.Label: A
Variants.Text: TC 003

Variants.Label: B
Variants.Text: TC 005

Variants.Label: C
Variants.Text: TC 002

Variants.Label: D
Variants.Text: TC 001

Explanation:
A) Is correct. 

Test TC 001 must come first, followed by TC 002, to satisfy dependencies. 
Afterwards, TC 003 to satisfy priority and then TC 004, followed by TC 005.

Question:
Consider the following test categories (1-4) and agile testing quadrants (A-D): 

1. Usability testing 
2. Component testing 
3. Functional testing 4. Reliability testing 

A. Agile testing quadrant Q1: technology facing, supporting the development team 
B. Agile testing quadrant Q2: business facing, supporting the development team 
C. Agile testing quadrant Q3: business facing, critique the product 
D. Agile testing quadrant Q4: technology facing, critique the product 

How do the following test categories map onto the agile testing quadrants?
Explanation:
A is correct. 

Considering: 
Usability testing is in Q3 (1 – C) 
Component testing is in Q1 (2 – A) 
Functional testing is in Q2 (3 – B) 
Reliability testing is in Q4 (4 – D)

Question:
During a risk analysis the following risk was identified and assessed: 

• Risk: Response time is too long to generate a report 
• Risk likelihood: medium; risk impact: high

Variants.Label: B
Variants.Text: Contingency plan

Variants.Label: C

Question: Which work product can be used by an agile team to show the amount of work that has been completed and the amount of total work remaining for a given iteration?

Variants.Label: A
Variants.Text: Acceptance criteria

Variants.Label: B
Variants.Text: Defect report

Variants.Label: C
Variants.Text: Test completion report

Variants.Label: D
Variants.Text: Burndown chart

Question: You need to update one of the automated test scripts to be in line with a new requirement. Which process indicates that you create a new version of the test script in the test repository?

Variants.Label: A
Variants.Text: Traceability management

Variants.Label: B
Variants.Text: Maintenance testing

Variants.Label: C
Variants.Text: Configuration management

Variants.Label: D
Variants.Text: Requirements engineering

Explanation: C) Is correct. To support testing, configuration management may involve the version control of all test items

Question:
You received the following defect report from the developers stating that the anomaly described in this test report is not reproducible. 

Application hangs up 

2022-May-03 – John Doe – Rejected

Question: Which test activity does a data preparation tool support?

Variants.Label: A
Variants.Text: Test monitoring and control

Variants.Label: B
Variants.Text: Test analysis

Variants.Label: C
Variants.Text: Test design and implementation

Variants.Label: D

Question: Which item correctly identifies a potential risk of performing test automation?

Variants.Label: A
Variants.Text: It may introduce unknown regressions in production

Variants.Label: B
Variants.Text: Sufficient efforts to maintain testware may not be properly allocated

Variants.Label: C
Variants.Text: Testing tools and associated testware may not be sufficiently relied upon

Variants.Label: D
Variants.Text: It may reduce the time allocated for manual testing

Question:
You were given a task to analyze and fix causes of failures in a new system to be released. 

Which activity are you performing?

Variants.Label: A
Variants.Text: Debugging

Variants.Label: B
Variants.Text: Software testing

Variants.Label: C
Variants.Text: Requirement elicitation

Variants.Label: D
Variants.Text: Defect management

Question: In many software organizations the test department is called the Quality Assurance (QA) department. Is this sentence correct or not and why?

Variants.Label: A
Variants.Text: It is correct. Testing and QA mean exactly the same thing

Variants.Label: B
Variants.Text: It is correct. These names can be used interchangeably because both testing and QA focus their activities on the same quality issues

Variants.Label: C
Variants.Text: It is not correct. Testing is something more; testing includes all activities with regard to quality. QA focuses on quality-related processes

Variants.Label: D
Variants.Text: It is not correct. QA is focused on quality-related processes while testing concentrates on demonstrating that a component or system is fit for purpose and to detect defects

Explanation:
D) Is correct. 

Considering: 
Testing and quality assurance are not the same. Testing is the process consisting of all software development lifecycle (SDLC) activities, both static and dynamic, concerned with planning, preparation and evaluation of a component or system and related work products to determine that they satisfy specified requirements, to demonstrate that they are fit for purpose and to detect defects. Quality assurance is focused on establishing, introducing, monitoring, improving, and adhering to the quality-related processes.

Question:
A wine storage system uses a control device that measures the wine cell temperature T (measured in °C, rounded to the nearest degree) and alarms the user if it deviates from the optimal value of 12, according to the following rules: 

• if T = 12, the system says, “optimal temperature” 
• if T < 12, the system says, “temperature is too low!” 
• if T > 12, the system says, “temperature is too high!” 

You want to use the 3-point boundary value analysis (BVA) to verify the behavior of the control device. A test input is a temperature in °C provided by the device. 

What is the MINIMAL set of test inputs that achieves 100% of the desired coverage?
Explanation:
C) Is correct. 

There are three equivalence partitions: {..., 10, 11}, {12}, and {13, 14, ...}. 
The boundary values are 11, 12 and 13. In the three-point boundary value analysis for each boundary, we need to test the boundary and both its neighbors, so: 
• for 11 we test 10, 11, 12 
• for 12 we test 11, 12, 13 
• for 13 we test 12, 13, 14 
Altogether we need to test 10, 11, 12, 13, and 14
